# Recipes {.unnumbered}

Short, copyable code for the changes you will make most often. Each recipe assumes you already have a plot stored as `p`, or a data frame `df` with a categorical column `group` and a numeric column `value`. Replace the names with your own.

In Python, these recipes assume `import pandas as pd` and `from plotnine import *`.

## Sort bars by value

Turn alphabetical order into a ranking.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```r
ggplot(df, aes(x = value, y = fct_reorder(group, value))) +
  geom_col()
```

## Python

```python
order = df.sort_values("value")["group"]
df["group"] = pd.Categorical(df["group"], categories=order)

(ggplot(df, aes(x="group", y="value"))
 + geom_col()
 + coord_flip())
```
:::

## Grey everything, highlight one group

Create a true or false column for the group your message is about.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```r
df |>
  mutate(focus = group == "Mine") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = value, y = fct_reorder(group, value), fill = focus)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey75", "#D6083B"), guide = "none")
```

## Python

```python
df["focus"] = df["group"] == "Mine"

(ggplot(df, aes(x="group", y="value", fill="focus"))
 + geom_col()
 + coord_flip()
 + scale_fill_manual(values=["#BFBFBF", "#D6083B"], guide=None))
```
:::

## Headline, subtitle, caption and axis labels



::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```r
p + labs(title = "What the reader should notice",
         subtitle = "What is measured, where and when",
         caption = "Source: ...",
         x = "Readable label (units)", y = NULL)
```

## Python

```python
p + labs(title="What the reader should notice",
         subtitle="What is measured, where and when",
         caption="Source: ...",
         x="Readable label (units)", y="")
```
:::

## Label line ends instead of a legend

Make a table of the last point of each line, and draw the labels there.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```r
ends <- df |> filter(year == max(year))

ggplot(df, aes(x = year, y = value, colour = group)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_text(data = ends, aes(label = group), hjust = 0, nudge_x = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.25))) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Python

```python
ends = df[df["year"] == df["year"].max()]

(ggplot(df, aes(x="year", y="value", color="group"))
 + geom_line()
 + geom_text(ends, aes(label="group"), ha="left", nudge_x=1)
 + theme(legend_position="none"))
```
:::

## Remove the legend



::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```r
p + theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Python

```python
p + theme(legend_position="none")
```
:::

## Colour-blind safe colours

The Okabe and Ito palette. Use a named vector or dictionary to fix colours to groups.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```r
cols <- c(A = "#E69F00", B = "#56B4E9", C = "#009E73", D = "#0072B2")
p + scale_colour_manual(values = cols)
```

## Python

```python
cols = {"A": "#E69F00", "B": "#56B4E9", "C": "#009E73", "D": "#0072B2"}
p + scale_color_manual(values=cols)
```
:::

## Viridis for continuous colour



::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```r
p + scale_colour_viridis_c()     # or scale_fill_viridis_c()
```

## Python

```python
p + scale_color_cmap("viridis")  # or scale_fill_cmap("viridis")
```
:::

## Diverging colours around zero



::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```r
p + scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#0072B2", mid = "white", high = "#D55E00",
                         midpoint = 0)
```

## Python

```python
p + scale_fill_gradient2(low="#0072B2", mid="white", high="#D55E00",
                         midpoint=0)
```
:::

## Readable tick labels



::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```r
p + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent())
p + scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma())
p + scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_dollar(accuracy = 1))
```

## Python

```python
p + scale_y_continuous(labels=lambda b: [f"{v:.0%}" for v in b])
p + scale_x_continuous(labels=lambda b: [f"{v:,.0f}" for v in b])
p + scale_x_log10(labels=lambda b: [f"${v:,.0f}" for v in b])
```
:::

## Zoom without removing data



::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```r
p + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(40, 90))
```

## Python

```python
p + coord_cartesian(ylim=(40, 90))
```
:::

## Small multiples with context

Draw all the data in grey behind every panel, then each group on top.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```r
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point(data = select(df, -group), colour = "grey85") +
  geom_point(colour = "#0072CF") +
  facet_wrap(~ group)
```

## Python

```python
background = df.drop(columns="group")

(ggplot(df, aes(x="x", y="y"))
 + geom_point(data=background, color="#D9D9D9")
 + geom_point(color="#0072CF")
 + facet_wrap("group"))
```
:::

## Clean theme with larger text



::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```r
p + theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

## Python

```python
p + theme_minimal(base_size=14) + theme(panel_grid_minor=element_blank())
```
:::

## Combine plots with panel letters



::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```r
library(patchwork)
(p1 | p2) / p3 + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
```

## Python

```python
p1 = p1 + labs(tag="A")
p2 = p2 + labs(tag="B")
p3 = p3 + labs(tag="C")
(p1 | p2) / p3
```
:::

## Save at the final size

8.5 cm is about one journal column; 17 cm is a full page width.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```r
ggsave("figures/figure1.pdf", p, width = 8.5, height = 6, units = "cm")
ggsave("figures/figure1.png", p, width = 8.5, height = 6, units = "cm", dpi = 600)
```

## Python

```python
p.save("figures/figure1.pdf", width=8.5, height=6, units="cm")
p.save("figures/figure1.png", width=8.5, height=6, units="cm", dpi=600)
```
:::
